explanation: Class templates in C++ enable the creation of generic classes that can work with different data types, promoting code reuse and flexibility. This is a core technique in modern C++ programming, as seen in the Standard Template Library (STL). In real-world scenarios, class templates are used for containers, algorithms, and utilities that need to handle various types without rewriting code. Best practices include defining template classes in header files to ensure proper instantiation during compilation, using meaningful template parameters, and adding constraints (e.g., via concepts in C++20+) for better error messages and type safety. Common pitfalls include forgetting that templates are not compiled until instantiated, which can lead to linker errors if definitions are not visible; avoid this by keeping template definitions in headers and testing with multiple types.
keywords: C++ templates, Class templates, Generic programming
